# Raw HTML in React dangerouslySetInnerHTML (review)

`qualor:js/react-dangerous-html` · Security hotspot · Severity: Medium · [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

> **Security hotspot.** This rule asks for a review: it marks code that is often safe and
> sometimes not, and a person decides which. A hotspot never fails the quality gate.

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Raw HTML given to React's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, in JSX or in `createElement()` props, whether
the `{ __html: ... }` object is written in the prop or built first. HTML that is visibly safe is not
reported: string constants, and HTML sanitised with DOMPurify or sanitize-html.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
React escapes everything it renders, except what goes through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. If any
part of that HTML comes from users (props, fetched data, stored content, Markdown rendered to HTML),
a `<script>` or an `onerror` attribute in it runs in the page, with the user's session.

Often the HTML is trusted (your own CMS, a constant, sanitised content), so this is a hotspot: check
where the HTML comes from.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a comment's HTML body is rendered as it is.

```jsx
import React from 'react';

export function Comment({ comment }) {
  return <div className="comment" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: comment.body }} />;
}
```

**Compliant:** the HTML is sanitised with DOMPurify first.

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';

export function Comment({ comment }) {
  return (
    <div className="comment" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment.body) }} />
  );
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Render text as children (`<p>{comment.body}</p>`); React escapes it.
- If HTML is needed, sanitise it: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` or `sanitize-html`.
- For JSON-LD in a `<script>` tag, escape `<`:
  `JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g, '\\u003c')`.
- If the HTML is trusted (a constant or your own build output), the code can stay as it is.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- React
- Next.js

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- The markup object is found where it is written (in the prop, assigned to a variable, returned, or
  in `createElement` props); one passed in from props or another module is not followed to the
  prop.
- DOMPurify is recognised through an import of `dompurify` or `isomorphic-dompurify`; an instance
  made with `DOMPurify(window)` is not, so its `sanitize()` result is reported.
- A variable assigned from `DOMPurify.sanitize()` or sanitize-html counts as sanitised even when it
  is changed later (`clean = clean + raw`).
- Constants are recognised only in the same file; constants imported from other modules are
  reported.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
